description: Thrust (C64, Firebird 1986) level data extracted from RAM; see re/report_levels.md

coordinate_system.x: world x unit = 4 hires pixels = 2 multicolour pixels; 0..255 (ship $09, objects, terrain)
coordinate_system.y: world row = 2 raster lines; ship $0C:$0B, objects; terrain row y drawn on raster line 2*y only
coordinate_system.screen: camera_x = $62 (left edge in units), camera_row = $04:$03; visible x in [camera_x, camera_x+80), visible rows y in [camera_row+65, camera_row+156) (bitmap lines 18..198, raster 66..246)
coordinate_system.object_sprite: hires 24x21 sprite, top-left at world px (4*x, 2*y+2)
coordinate_system.ship_sprite: no pod attached: top-left at world px (4*ship_x + 6, 2*ship_y - 18) (offset $24/$26 = 0/-10 rows)
coordinate_system.directions: 0..31, 0 = up, increasing clockwise (same as ship angle $0D)
coordinate_system.horizontal_wrap: camera_x is kept in 1..175: if it becomes >=176 (and <216) everything (camera, ship, bullets) is shifted by -175 units; if 0 or >=216 by +175. Terrain/objects are NOT periodic.

object_types.7: switch (sprite $2C, ")" shape: mounted on a LEFT wall, bulge points right)
object_types.8: switch (sprite $2D, "(" shape: mounted on a RIGHT wall, bulge points left)

units.world_px: px_x = 4*x, px_y = 2*y (hires pixel space, C64 pixel aspect)

terrain.format: open_spans: one [L, R] per row y = 0..height-1; x is open (empty) iff L <= x < R, everything else (and every row >= height) is solid rock. Rows are drawn only on the even raster line 2*y; line 2*y+1 is always blank. Doors are applied CLOSED here.

doors.formula: L = 174 - o for every door row
doors.animation: shooting any switch sets timer t($6B)=255; t decrements by 1 every game frame while >0. Each game frame (only while the door is inside the row buffer, see active_when): if t >= 16: o = min(o+1, 16) else o = t. o($6C)=0 closed, 16=fully open. Both are 0 after level start / restart.
